Vitamin C Serums: A Practical Buying and Using Guide

Forms, percentages, packaging and when to apply, so you can choose a vitamin C that works and lasts.

By GlowHer Editorial Team · 16 October 2026

Educational content only, not medical advice. Some pages may contain affiliate links. Read our disclosure.

In this article

  1. Forms and strengths
  2. Check the packaging
  3. How to use it
  4. What it pairs with

Vitamin C is an antioxidant that can help skin look brighter and more even, and it complements sunscreen in a morning routine.

Forms and strengths

  • L-ascorbic acid (10 to 20 percent) is the most studied form but is also the most unstable and can sting.
  • Derivatives (such as ascorbyl glucoside or magnesium ascorbyl phosphate) are gentler and more stable, though sometimes less potent.

Check the packaging

Vitamin C breaks down with light and air. Choose opaque, airtight packaging, such as a pump, and note any expiry guidance. A serum that has turned dark orange or brown has oxidised.

How to use it

  1. Apply to clean, dry skin in the morning.
  2. Follow with moisturizer, then sunscreen.
  3. If skin is sensitive, start every other day.

What it pairs with

Vitamin C works well with sunscreen, vitamin E and hyaluronic acid. If you use exfoliating acids or retinol, many people keep those for the evening to simplify things.
